what_its_for: Apremilast is used to treat moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (a skin condition that causes red, scaly patches), psoriatic arthritis (joint pain and swelling related to psoriasis), and mouth sores (oral ulcers) in adults with Behçet's disease. It works by reducing inflammation in your body.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. Do not crush, split, or chew the tablet. Try to take it at the same times each day — once in the morning and once in the evening, about 12 hours apart. When you first start this medicine, you will follow a special 'starter pack' schedule that slowly increases your dose over 5 days to help reduce stomach side effects.
dosing: The usual dose is 30 mg twice daily (once in the morning and once in the evening). However, when you first start taking apremilast, you will use a starter pack that gradually increases your dose over the first 5 days: Day 1 — 10 mg in the morning only; Day 2 — 10 mg morning and 10 mg evening; Day 3 — 10 mg morning and 20 mg evening; Day 4 — 20 mg morning and 20 mg evening; Day 5 — 20 mg morning and 30 mg evening; Day 6 and beyond — 30 mg morning and 30 mg evening. If you have severe kidney problems, your doctor may lower your dose to 30 mg once daily.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular scheduled time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store apremilast at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking apremilast with strong medicines that speed up the breakdown of drugs in your liver (called strong CYP450 inducers), such as rifampin (an antibiotic), phenobarbital, carbamazepine, or phenytoin (seizure medicines), because these can make apremilast less effective. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before starting any new prescription medicines, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or herbal supplements. Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as it may worsen side effects like nausea or dizziness.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: new or worsening feelings of depression, anxiety, or sadness; thoughts of self-harm or suicide; severe or ongoing diarrhea, nausea, or vomiting that does not get better; unexplained weight loss; severe allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, difficulty breathing). Also let your doctor know if you become pregnant or plan to become pregnant while taking this medicine.
when_it_works: Most people start to notice some improvement within a few weeks, but it may take up to 4 to 6 months to see the full benefit of apremilast. Keep taking your medicine even if you don't notice changes right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Apremilast is not recommended during pregnancy because it may harm the unborn baby. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using this medicine. Kidney problems: If you have severe kidney disease, your dose will be lowered to 30 mg once daily. Elderly patients: No dose adjustment is needed for older adults, but they may be more sensitive to side effects. Children: Apremilast is not approved for use in patients under 18 years of age.
